operations.current_value:
For every admitted closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ of an isolated compound, assume its declared outer boundary is isolated throughout, its material constitution is fixed, its center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and both endpoint preparations are equilibrium macrostates. Include every named auxiliary and work device in the compound. Fix the finite constituent split $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ used for the endpoint bookkeeping, with $m\in\mathbb N$, $m\ge1$, and constitutions $c_1,\ldots,c_m$. The split accounts for every constituent whose entropy can change; any included auxiliary not represented in it must have an explicitly model-declared zero entropy change between these endpoints. Its endpoint product is

$$\mathcal D:=D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m},\qquad \mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D,$$

where $\mathcal F$ is the model-declared feasible endpoint set for the fixed totals, retained barriers, and permitted exchanges, as in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The process model supplies an endpoint association on the two formal endpoint labels $-$ and $+$:

$$\rho_P:\{-,+\}\longrightarrow\mathcal F,\qquad \rho_P(-)=\mathbf x_P^-=(x_{1,P}^-,\ldots,x_{m,P}^-),\qquad \rho_P(+)=\mathbf x_P^+=(x_{1,P}^+,\ldots,x_{m,P}^+),$$

where $\mathbf x_P^-$ and $\mathbf x_P^+$ are respectively the declared constituent-state tuples representing the aggregate equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$ of $P$. Both tuples must belong to the same $\mathcal F$. Restrict to endpoint splits admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems, so that its additive entropy rule applies. On this admitted $\mathcal F$, define

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i)\qquad\left(\mathbf x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathcal F\right).$$

This uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]].

The adopted macroscopic second law is

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))\ge0.$$

The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))=0$. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

For every admitted closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ of an isolated compound, assume its declared outer boundary is isolated throughout, its material constitution is fixed, its center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change, and both endpoint preparations are equilibrium macrostates. Every additional named auxiliary or work device has an endpoint set $Y_j$, energy map, and adopted entropy map $S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}$ as in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. Every constituent whose entropy can change must occur either in the thermodynamic split or through one of these explicit auxiliary maps. Every auxiliary is retained in the complete endpoint tuples and energy constraints. An explicitly entropy-neutral device may be assigned $S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}=0$; more generally an auxiliary with declared zero endpoint entropy change cancels in the displayed inequality, while its variable state and energy remain in $\mathcal F$. Its endpoint product is

$$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}}:=(D_{c_1}\times\cdots\times D_{c_m})\times Y_1\times\cdots\times Y_k,\qquad \mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{all}},$$

where $\mathcal F$ is the model-declared feasible endpoint set for the fixed totals, retained barriers, and permitted exchanges, as in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The process model supplies an endpoint association on the two formal endpoint labels $-$ and $+$:

$$\rho_P:\{-,+\}\longrightarrow\mathcal F,\qquad \rho_P(-)=\mathbf x_P^-=(x_{1,P}^-,\ldots,x_{m,P}^-,y_{1,P}^-,\ldots,y_{k,P}^-),\qquad \rho_P(+)=\mathbf x_P^+=(x_{1,P}^+,\ldots,x_{m,P}^+,y_{1,P}^+,\ldots,y_{k,P}^+),$$

where $\mathbf x_P^-$ and $\mathbf x_P^+$ are respectively the declared constituent-state tuples including all auxiliary endpoint states and representing the aggregate equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$ of $P$. Both tuples must belong to the same $\mathcal F$. Restrict to endpoint splits admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] as a collection of independent separated macroscopic systems, so that its additive entropy rule applies to the macroscopic split; additionally adopt additivity of the explicitly modeled auxiliary entropy contributions for the complete compound. For $k=0$ this is the original thermodynamic-only split. On this admitted $\mathcal F$, define

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i)+\sum_{j=1}^{k}S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}(y_j)\qquad\left(\mathbf x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m,y_1,\ldots,y_k)\in\mathcal F\right).$$

This uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]].

The adopted macroscopic second law is

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))\ge0.$$

The process record and the zero-change conditions are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The process may pass through nonequilibrium configurations; this postulate compares endpoint entropies only and assigns no entropy function to those intermediate configurations.

For an admitted reversible operation in the sense of [[def-td-reversible-process]], adopt $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(+))-S_{\mathrm{tot}}(\rho_P(-))=0$. An admitted irreversible adiabatic operation may have a strictly positive entropy increase, but strict increase is not required for every irreversible operation. The postulate does not state monotonicity for an open compound, an externally driven process, a subsystem that exchanges energy with an omitted environment, or every microscopic trajectory.

operations.current_value:
Let $\mathcal F$ be the explicitly declared feasible endpoint set of an isolated compound whose constituents are independent separated macroscopic systems, as defined in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For this route, adopt the physical criterion that any endpoint tuple the model classifies as a stable equilibrium under these fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges satisfies

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i),$$

Here $\max$ means that $x^{\mathrm{eq}}\in\mathcal F$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})\ge S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$, using maximum in the sense of [[def-max-min]]. The finite sum is as in [[def-finite-sum]], and the summands are those of the separated macroscopic constituents under [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. Whenever the stable-equilibrium label is used, attainment is assumed: at least one maximizing endpoint lies in $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F$ is empty or the entropy supremum is not attained, this item supplies no equilibrium state.

“Global” refers to every endpoint in this exact $\mathcal F$, not just nearby states, states reachable by a restricted short-time dynamics, or states on a selected branch. A local maximum that is not global, or a long-lived preparation trapped by kinetic barriers, is not declared stable equilibrium by this postulate. No uniqueness or relaxation dynamics is assumed.
operations.proposed_value:
Let $\mathcal F$ be the explicitly declared feasible endpoint set of an isolated compound with the chosen independent separated macroscopic subsystem split and any explicitly modeled named auxiliaries, as defined in [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For this route, adopt the physical criterion that any endpoint tuple the model classifies as a stable equilibrium under these fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges satisfies

$$S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})=\max_{x\in\mathcal F}S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x),\qquad S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x):=\sum_{i=1}^{m}S_{c_i}(x_i)+\sum_{j=1}^{k}S_j^{\mathrm{aux}}(y_j),$$

Here $\max$ means that $x^{\mathrm{eq}}\in\mathcal F$ and $S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x^{\mathrm{eq}})\ge S_{\mathrm{tot}}(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal F$, using maximum in the sense of [[def-max-min]]. Here $x=(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)$ is a complete endpoint tuple from [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]; $k=0$ gives the original thermodynamic-only formula. The finite sums are as in [[def-finite-sum]]. The macroscopic summands are those of the separated constituents under [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], and any auxiliary summands are the explicitly adopted endpoint entropy maps of the same complete compound model. This route assumes that these contributions add for the complete admitted split. A constant auxiliary entropy may be dropped as an additive constant when comparing maxima, whereas variable auxiliary entropy must be retained. Whenever the stable-equilibrium label is used, attainment is assumed: at least one maximizing endpoint lies in $\mathcal F$. If $\mathcal F$ is empty or the entropy supremum is not attained, this item supplies no equilibrium state.

“Global” refers to every endpoint in this exact $\mathcal F$, not just nearby states, states reachable by a restricted short-time dynamics, or states on a selected branch. A local maximum that is not global, or a long-lived preparation trapped by kinetic barriers, is not declared stable equilibrium by this postulate. No uniqueness or relaxation dynamics is assumed.

operations.current_value:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and let $H$ be a separable
complex Hilbert space, with separability taken in its Hilbert norm topology
as defined in [[def-separable-space]], and with the second-variable-linear convention of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ define the bosonic
creation and annihilation maps $a^\dagger(h)$ and $a(h)$ and the fermionic maps
$c^\dagger(h)$ and $c(h)$ as in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Write $a_n(h)$ and $a_n^\dagger(h)$ for
their restrictions to the $n$th bosonic sector. For bosons set

$$D(a(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge1}\|a_n(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad D(a^\dagger(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge0}\|a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$

Then $\mathcal F_s(H)$ and $\mathcal F_a(H)$ are Hilbert spaces,
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is dense, and it is a graph core for both maximal
bosonic sector maps. The bosonic operators on their displayed domains are
closed and mutually adjoint, and on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ satisfy

$$[a(h),a^\dagger(k)]=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad [a(h),a(k)]=[a^\dagger(h),a^\dagger(k)]=0.$$

The fermionic $c(h)$ and $c^\dagger(h)$ extend to bounded operators on the
whole Fock space, with norms $\|h\|$, and satisfy on the whole space

$$\{c(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad \{c(h),c(k)\}=\{c^\dagger(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=0.$$

This is a mathematical construction of the two Fock representations; it does
not assign particle statistics to a physical species.
